essay_hooks.hook_text: It is a fine winter morning in 2025. As commuters travel to work, the metro rail crashes to a grinding halt. Concurrently, planes in the airspace lose communication with ground control. Banks report breach of confidential data. Government websites are hacked with threatening messages. Energy and nuclear power plant control systems are infected with strange viruses. Within an hour, critical infrastructure collapses as the country falls victim to a coordinated cyberattack—cyberwar. This scary scenario, confined earlier to sci-fi movies, is now a potential reality of the 21st century...
essay_hooks.subject: Essay Evaluator

essay_hooks.hook_text: It was 1893. A bright young lawyer was travelling first class on a train in South Africa. During the journey, a white man objected to his presence despite his valid ticket, insisting 'coloured' men were supposed to ride in third class. When the lawyer refused to give up his seat, he was thrown off the train at Pietermaritzburg. Insulted at this discrimination, the young man resolved to fight injustice with truth and non-violence. He went on to become the force of change he wished to see in the world: Mahatma Gandhi.
essay_hooks.subject: Essay Evaluator

essay_hooks.theme: Change is the End Result of All Learning
essay_hooks.hook_text: In the 1980s, the Govt of Tamil Nadu faced a crisis: school dropout rates were unacceptably high. A detailed study revealed that ill-health and acute malnutrition were the primary causes. The state government decided to introduce a unique scheme—the now popular mid-day meal scheme. Within a couple of years, education levels started rising and dropout ratios fell sharply. As Jean Dreze observes, the mid-day meal scheme remains the primary reason for Tamil Nadu's stellar primary education performance. This incident proves that change is the end result of all learning.
essay_hooks.subject: Essay Evaluator

essay_hooks.hook_text: Around 1 million plant and animal species are on the verge of extinction, with alarming implications for human survival, according to a United Nations report. Our natural resources are getting depleted, rains are getting erratic, and the air is turning toxic. The scientific consensus is clear: carbon emissions from human activities are irrevocably damaging the environment at a rapid pace. It is not climate change anymore—it is a climate emergency.
essay_hooks.subject: Essay Evaluator

essay_rhetorical_conclusions.subject: Essay Evaluator

essay_rhetorical_conclusions.ending_text: Going by Gandhiji's Talisman, the ultimate measure to determine whether our economic and technological endeavours are successful is not to see how far we launch rockets or how tall we build skyscrapers. The ultimate test is to check whether it restores control over destiny to the poorest of the poor.
essay_rhetorical_conclusions.subject: Essay Evaluator

essay_rhetorical_conclusions.ending_text: Recalling the opening story of farmer Narayana: 'Technology and policy reforms must ultimately converge to light up the life of Narayana. When every citizen gains food for the mouth, work for the hand, and a spark of joy in their eyes, India will truly realize its vision.'
essay_rhetorical_conclusions.subject: Essay Evaluator

essay_rhetorical_conclusions.ending_text: Achieving a 5 trillion economy is challenging, yet possible. But we must ask ourselves—to what end? A superpower status must be about making a positive difference to every citizen of the republic, realizing the Preamble's sacred promise of securing justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity for all.
essay_rhetorical_conclusions.subject: Essay Evaluator
